Title: Public health information page tutorial — Lily Design System

Description: Build a public health service's medicine page, step by step, with SvelteKit and Lily: a header with the service's mark and search, breadcrumbs, a lede, inset text, urgent advice cards, review dates and a footer.

# Public health information page tutorial

Build the kind of page a public health service publishes about a medicine, in the shape such services use, with SvelteKit and Lily.

## What you'll build

A medicine page for paracetamol, laid out as public health services lay theirs out: the service's header with its mark, a search field and a menu; breadcrumbs and a back link; the medicine's name, its common brands and a lede; sections with lists, inset text, urgent advice and an important note; the dates the page was reviewed and will be next; and a footer. About 40 minutes.

The finished page on a wide screen. At a phone's width.

**For learning only.** Every sentence on the page is placeholder text, not medical advice. The structure is what the tutorial teaches; a real page's words come from its clinical authors.

## Whose look this is

The page wears Lily's NHS England patient theme, and its layout follows the medicine pages public health services publish. It is not any service's page. Its service, Example Health, is fictional, with a mark drawn for this tutorial, and it names no real service or country: a theme lends a look, never another body's identity ([visual identity](https://github.com/LilyDesignSystem/lily-design-system/blob/main/AGENTS/visual-identity.md)). One of the tests checks it.

## Before you start

You need Node 26, pnpm, and a little Svelte: the [Svelte tutorial](https://lilydesignsystem.com/tutorials/svelte/) is enough. Make the app, then add Lily:

```
npx sv create health-page --template minimal --types ts --no-add-ons --install pnpm
cd health-page
pnpm add @lilydesignsystem/svelte-headless @lilydesignsystem/themes
pnpm add -D vitest
```

Each code block below is one whole file, under the path shown above it. Copy it as it is, replacing the file if the new app already has one.

```
// The page's content, as data. The structure follows a public health service's medicine page; the text is placeholder text, so
// nothing here is advice. A real page's words come from its clinical authors, with a review date.

export type Block =
  | { kind: "p"; text: string }
  | { kind: "list"; items: string[] }
  | { kind: "inset"; text: string; link?: { text: string; href: string } }
  | { kind: "urgent"; heading: string; items: string[]; after?: string }
  | { kind: "important"; heading: string; text: string };

export interface Part {
  heading: string;
  blocks: Block[];
}

export interface Section {
  heading: string;
  blocks: Block[];
  parts?: Part[];
}

export interface Medicine {
  name: string;
  brands: string;
  lede: string;
  intro: Block[];
  sections: Section[];
  /** YYYY-MM-DD: a calendar date. */
  lastReviewed: string;
  /** How often the page is reviewed, in whole years. */
  reviewEvery: number;
}
```

## Step 2: The rules, with tests

A page with no logic still has rules: when its next review is due, how a date is written, and the id each heading gives its section. A date is a calendar date, so it is written in UTC and no time zone moves it a day; a 29 February lands on 28 February in a year with none; and a date that is not a real day is an error, never a quiet guess.

`src/lib/page.ts`

```
// The page's rules, as pure functions with tests: when the next review is due, how a date is written, and the id a section's
// heading gives its anchor. Bad input is an error, never a quiet guess.

export class PageError extends Error {
  readonly reason: "date" | "years";
  constructor(reason: "date" | "years", message: string) {
    super(message);
    this.reason = reason;
  }
}

function parts(iso: string): [number, number, number] {
  const m = /^(\d{4})-(\d{2})-(\d{2})$/.exec(iso);
  if (!m) throw new PageError("date", `${iso} is not YYYY-MM-DD`);
  const [year, month, day] = [Number(m[1]), Number(m[2]), Number(m[3])];
  const date = new Date(Date.UTC(year, month - 1, day));
  if (date.getUTCMonth() !== month - 1 || date.getUTCDate() !== day) throw new PageError("date", `${iso} is not a real day`);
  return [year, month, day];
}

const leap = (year: number) => (year % 4 === 0 && year % 100 !== 0) || year % 400 === 0;

/** The date `years` whole years after `iso`. A 29 February lands on 28 February in a year with none. */
export function addYears(iso: string, years: number): string {
  if (!Number.isInteger(years) || years < 0) throw new PageError("years", `${years} is not a whole number of years`);
  const [year, month, given] = parts(iso);
  let day = given;
  const to = year + years;
  if (month === 2 && day === 29 && !leap(to)) day = 28;
  return `${String(to).padStart(4, "0")}-${String(month).padStart(2, "0")}-${String(day).padStart(2, "0")}`;
}

/** A date as the site's readers write it: "24 March 2026". In UTC, so no time zone moves a calendar date a day. */
export function longDate(iso: string, locale: string): string {
  const [year, month, day] = parts(iso);
  return new Intl.DateTimeFormat(locale, { dateStyle: "long", timeZone: "UTC" }).format(Date.UTC(year, month - 1, day));
}

/** The id a heading gives its section, for a link to it: lower case, words joined by hyphens. */
export function sectionId(heading: string): string {
  return heading
    .toLowerCase()
    .replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, "-")
    .replace(/^-|-$/g, "");
}
```

The tests also check the content names no real service or country.

`src/lib/page.test.ts`

```
import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
import { paracetamol } from "./content.js";
import { addYears, longDate, PageError, sectionId } from "./page.js";
import { words } from "./words.js";

describe("the page's rules", () => {
  it("adds whole years to a review date", () => {
    expect(addYears("2026-03-24", 3)).toBe("2029-03-24");
    expect(addYears("2026-03-24", 0)).toBe("2026-03-24");
  });

  it("lands a 29 February on 28 February in a year with none", () => {
    expect(addYears("2028-02-29", 1)).toBe("2029-02-28");
    expect(addYears("2028-02-29", 4)).toBe("2032-02-29");
  });

  it("refuses a date that is not a real day", () => {
    expect(() => addYears("2026-02-30", 1)).toThrow(PageError);
    expect(() => longDate("24/03/2026", "en-GB")).toThrow(expect.objectContaining({ reason: "date" }));
  });

  it("refuses years that are not whole and not negative", () => {
    for (const years of [-1, 1.5, Number.NaN]) {
      expect(() => addYears("2026-03-24", years)).toThrow(expect.objectContaining({ reason: "years" }));
    }
  });

  it("writes a date as the site's readers do", () => {
    expect(longDate("2026-03-24", "en-GB")).toBe("24 March 2026");
  });

  it("gives each heading an id for its anchor", () => {
    expect(sectionId("Who can and cannot take paracetamol")).toBe("who-can-and-cannot-take-paracetamol");
    expect(sectionId("Food, drink and alcohol with paracetamol")).toBe("food-drink-and-alcohol-with-paracetamol");
  });
});

describe("the content", () => {
  it("gives every section a different id", () => {
    const ids = paracetamol.sections.map((s) => sectionId(s.heading));
    expect(new Set(ids).size).toBe(ids.length);
  });

  it("names no real service or country: the service is fictional", () => {
    const text = JSON.stringify({ paracetamol, words });
    expect(text).not.toMatch(/\bNHS\b|\bUK\b|United Kingdom|England|\b111\b/);
  });
});
```

**Check your work:** run `pnpm vitest run`. All eight tests pass.

## Step 3: The service's frame

The service's mark goes in a link to its home page, named for the service, never "logo". The header is Lily's `Header` with the mark, a search form with Lily's `SearchInput`, and the menu; the footer is Lily's `Footer`. An amber line in the header says the page is an example, on every page.

The theme styles Lily's components; the service's own design is the app's: a band of the theme's primary colour behind the header, the page colours, and a readable column. It uses only the theme's custom properties, so another theme changes it too.

`src/app.css`

```
/* The service's own design, on top of the theme: a band of the theme's primary colour behind the header, the theme's page and
   link colours, and a readable column. Lily ships none of this; it is the app's, as a service's identity always is. */

body {
  margin: 0;
  background: var(--color-base-200);
  color: var(--color-base-content);
  font-family: var(--lily-font-body);
  line-height: var(--lily-line-height-body, 1.5);
}

.site-main a {

}

/* Urgent advice: its heading on a band of the theme's error colour, in that colour's own text colour. */

}

}

  padding: 0;
}

  padding: 0.5rem 1rem;

  color: var(--color-warning-content);
  font-weight: 700;
}

.site-header-row,
.site-nav ul,
.site-main,
.site-footer-lists,
.site-footer p {
  max-inline-size: 60rem;

}

.site-header-row {
  display: flex;
```

## Step 4: The blocks

Each kind of block is drawn with its Lily component: `InsetText` for a note beside the text, `CareCard` with `type="urgent"` for urgent advice, and `WarningCallout` for an important note.

`src/lib/components/Blocks.svelte`

```
<script lang="ts">
  import { CareCard, InsetText, WarningCallout } from "@lilydesignsystem/svelte-headless";
  import type { Block } from "#lib/content.js";

  // One block of content, each kind drawn with the Lily component made for it.
  let { blocks }: { blocks: Block[] } = $props();
</script>

{#each blocks as block, i (i)}
  {#if block.kind === "p"}
    <p>{block.text}</p>
  {:else if block.kind === "list"}
    <ul>
      {#each block.items as item (item)}<li>{item}</li>{/each}
    </ul>
  {:else if block.kind === "inset"}
    <InsetText>
      <p>{block.text}{#if block.link}{" "}<a href={block.link.href}>{block.link.text}</a>{/if}</p>
    </InsetText>
  {:else if block.kind === "urgent"}
    <CareCard type="urgent" heading={block.heading}>
      <ul>
        {#each block.items as item (item)}<li>{item}</li>{/each}
      </ul>
      {#if block.after}<p>{block.after}</p>{/if}
    </CareCard>
  {:else if block.kind === "important"}
    <WarningCallout label={block.heading}>
      <h3>{block.heading}</h3>
      <p>{block.text}</p>
    </WarningCallout>
  {/if}
{/each}
```

## Step 5: The pages

The medicine page: breadcrumbs and a back link, the name with its brands, the lede, then each section with an id from its heading, and the review dates in Lily's `ReviewDate`, a `<time>` with the machine-readable date.

`src/routes/medicines/paracetamol-for-adults/+page.svelte`

```
<script lang="ts">
  import {
    BackLink,
    BreadcrumbLink,
    BreadcrumbList,
    BreadcrumbListItem,
    BreadcrumbNav,
    ReviewDate,
  } from "@lilydesignsystem/svelte-headless";
  import Blocks from "#lib/components/Blocks.svelte";
  import { paracetamol as medicine } from "#lib/content.js";
  import { addYears, longDate, sectionId } from "#lib/page.js";
  import { words } from "#lib/words.js";

  const nextReview = addYears(medicine.lastReviewed, medicine.reviewEvery);
</script>

<svelte:head><title>{medicine.name} - {words.service}</title></svelte:head>

<BreadcrumbNav label={words.breadcrumbs}>
  <BreadcrumbList>
    <BreadcrumbListItem><BreadcrumbLink href="/">{words.homeCrumb}</BreadcrumbLink></BreadcrumbListItem>
    <BreadcrumbListItem><BreadcrumbLink href="/medicines/">{words.medicines}</BreadcrumbLink></BreadcrumbListItem>
  </BreadcrumbList>
</BreadcrumbNav>
<BackLink href="/medicines/">{words.back}</BackLink>

<article class="medicine">
  <h1>{medicine.name} <span class="medicine-brands">{medicine.brands}</span></h1>
  <p class="medicine-lede">{medicine.lede}</p>
  <Blocks blocks={medicine.intro} />

  {#each medicine.sections as section (section.heading)}
    <section aria-labelledby={sectionId(section.heading)}>
      <h2 id={sectionId(section.heading)}>{section.heading}</h2>
      <Blocks blocks={section.blocks} />
      {#each section.parts ?? [] as part (part.heading)}
        <h3>{part.heading}</h3>
        <Blocks blocks={part.blocks} />
      {/each}
    </section>
  {/each}

  <p class="medicine-review">
    {words.lastReviewed} <ReviewDate datetime={medicine.lastReviewed} label="">{longDate(medicine.lastReviewed, words.locale)}</ReviewDate><br />
    {words.nextReview} <ReviewDate datetime={nextReview} label="">{longDate(nextReview, words.locale)}</ReviewDate>
  </p>
</article>
```

## What this does not do yet

- Search goes nowhere, and most links go home: the medicine page is the lesson.
- The content is placeholder text in a TypeScript file. A real service keeps its pages in a content system, with authors, reviewers and the dates this page shows.
- It has one language. The words and the content are data, so another language is another copy of each.
